description: D-108 — an unknown extension point is an error; an empty one is not (spec v1.51.0, docs/features/extension-system.md '## An unknown extension point is an error; an empty one is not'). `get`, `get_all` and `unregister` MUST reject a point name that was never registered with InvalidInputError(code=GENERAL_INVALID_INPUT), and MUST NOT raise for a registered point that currently holds nothing. The two halves are load-bearing together: an SDK that answers null/empty/false for a misspelled name turns a typo into a wiring bug that first surfaces at apply(), and an SDK that raises for an empty point breaks every host that probes before registering. Runner: build a FRESH ExtensionManager per case, with the six built-in points ('discoverer', 'middleware', 'acl', 'span_exporter', 'module_validator', 'approval_handler') and nothing registered. For each name in `setup`, register one SDK-native extension of that point's declared type (any trivial instance will do; keep a reference to it). Then perform `operation` on `point_name`. `unregister_target` selects the object handed to `unregister`: 'setup' = the exact object registered by `setup` (same identity), 'stranger' = a freshly built extension of the same type that was NEVER registered. Assertions: when `expected.error_code` is a string the call MUST fail with the framework error carrying that code — an SDK that returns null / an empty collection / false instead is a FAILURE, and so is an SDK that raises a generic language error (KeyError, bare Error) that carries no code. When `expected.error_code` is null the call MUST NOT raise, and the remaining `expected` key is the answer: `value` is 'none' or 'present' for `get`, `count` is the length for `get_all`, `removed` is the boolean for `unregister`.
